h1: The 5 Best Ceramic Air Fryers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Ceramic Air Fryers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five air fryers with ceramic-coated baskets compared on capacity, cooking functions, presets and price band.
summary: The Cosori TurboBlaze is the best ceramic air fryer, a 6 quart, 9-in-1 model with a stated PFAS-free ceramic coating. The Cosori Pro LE is the value pick at 5 quarts, and the Nuwave Brio Plus gives 8 quarts. The Tastee adds 24 presets and app recipes, and the Chefman is the budget 8 quart.
intro: Ceramic on an air fryer label can mean very different things. Some listings say PFAS-free ceramic coating, others only say non-stick or non-toxic, and that difference decides whether the basket is actually ceramic. Read the coating line before you read the wattage, because a vague word on the box is where marketing most often outruns the spec.

We reviewed eight models and kept the five whose listings name a ceramic coating or ceramic basket. They are ranked on capacity, cooking functions, presets and price band, using the spec sheets alone. Capacity runs from 5 to 8 quarts, which is the figure that most changes daily use. A large basket suits a family but wastes counter space, while a small one forces you to cook in rounds. Prices span the $50 to $100 and $100 to $200 bands.

products.name: Cosori TurboBlaze Air Fryer
products.verdict: A 9-in-1 with a PFAS-free ceramic coating at a 6 quart size.
products.description:
The TurboBlaze is a 6 quart, 9-in-1 air fryer with a PFAS-free ceramic coating, in the $100 to $200 band. Nine functions usually means air fry, roast, bake, reheat and dehydrate among others, so it can replace a small oven or toaster oven for many jobs. The coating wording is the strongest in this group.

It ranks first because it combines a stated PFAS-free coating with the widest function count here. Against the Pro LE it adds capacity, six quarts instead of five, at a higher band. Against the Nuwave Brio Plus it gives up two quarts but offers far more listed cooking modes.

It suits families of three or four who want one machine for most jobs. The caveat is size: at 6 quarts it will not handle a crowd in one go, and it costs more than the Pro LE.
products.skipIf: You cook for a crowd every night.

products.name: Cosori Air Fryer Pro LE 5 Qt
products.verdict: The same 9 functions in a 5 quart body for less.
products.description:
The Pro LE is a 5 quart, 9-in-1 air fryer with a ceramic coating and a shake reminder, in the $50 to $100 band. The shake reminder is a useful nudge. Fries and wings crisp unevenly if the basket is never tossed, and a prompt makes that routine automatic.

It ranks below the TurboBlaze because it is a size smaller and the listing does not say PFAS-free, only ceramic. In return it costs a full band less and keeps the same nine functions. That is the best price-to-feature ratio in the group. It is also the smallest basket here.

Buy it for one to three people. The caveat is the coating wording: if PFAS-free matters to you, the TurboBlaze or Nuwave states it outright, and this listing does not.
products.skipIf: You batch cook for four or more.

products.name: Nuwave Brio Plus Air Fryer 8 Qt
products.verdict: An 8 quart basket with a PFAS-free ceramic coating.
products.description:
The Brio Plus offers 8 quarts of space and a PFAS-free ceramic coating, in the $100 to $200 band. Eight quarts means a whole batch of wings or a side of vegetables fits in one load, rather than two rounds, which saves time on busy nights. The model is described as new and improved.

It ranks below the Cosori models because the listing gives fewer details on cooking functions. What you gain is room: 8 quarts is the largest basket among the Cosoris and ties the Chefman. It also states PFAS-free, which the Chefman and the Pro LE do not. Larger baskets can cook less evenly, so shake or flip more often.

It suits bigger households that cook big batches. The caveat is counter space: it needs more room than a 5 or 6 quart, and the sparse function list leaves you guessing about extras.

products.name: Tastee Ceramic Air Fryer
products.verdict: 24 presets, in-app recipes and a dishwasher-safe basket.
products.description:
The Tastee is an 8-in-1, 5.5 quart air fryer with 24 one-touch presets, in-app recipes with a window and a dishwasher-safe non-stick basket, in the $100 to $200 band. Presets set time and temperature for common foods, and recipes in the app walk you through them.

It ranks fourth because you pay the same band as the TurboBlaze for fewer functions, though you get app recipes and a viewing window. The basket is described as dishwasher-safe and non-stick, but the wording is less specific about PFAS than the Cosori or Nuwave. It sits between the 5 and 6 quart models in size.

It suits beginners who want presets to guide them. The caveat is value: experienced cooks will use manual controls anyway, and the app adds little for them.

products.name: Chefman Crispinator Air Fryer 6-in-1 with 8 Qt capacity
products.verdict: An 8 quart basket with a ceramic basket, in a lower band.
products.description:
The Chefman Crispinator is a 6-in-1 air fryer with an 8 quart capacity, a nonstick ceramic basket and a viewing window, in the $50 to $100 band. An 8 quart basket at this band is the draw: it matches the Nuwave's capacity for a full band less.

It ranks last because it lists fewer cooking details than the others. Against the Nuwave 8 Qt it saves a band, but the Nuwave states PFAS-free and the Chefman names only a ceramic basket. The viewing window lets you check food without opening the drawer. Six functions covers the basics but trails the Cosori's nine.

It works for budget buyers who need space. The caveat is coating wording: only the basket is stated as ceramic, so check the listing for what covers the rest of the interior.
products.skipIf: You want the strongest feature set.

whatMatters.detail: Ceramic is a coating applied to the basket, replacing traditional non-stick chemistry. Some listings say PFAS-free, while others only say non-toxic. Choose a model that names ceramic explicitly. Search the bullet points for the word ceramic, and for PFAS-free if that matters to you, and ignore generic phrases like non-toxic. The TurboBlaze and Nuwave state it, while the Chefman names only the basket.

Capacity in quarts sets how much food fits in one batch. Five quarts feeds two or three, while eight feeds a crowd. Too large wastes counter space and heats slowly, and too small forces two rounds. Match it to your household and counter. Here, the Pro LE is 5 quarts, the TurboBlaze 6, the Tastee 5.5, and the Nuwave and Chefman 8.

A 9-in-1 usually bakes, roasts, reheats and dehydrates as well as air fries. More functions help if you want to replace other appliances. Look at the named modes, not the count alone, because a count can include trivial variations of the same heating mode. The Cosori models list nine, the Tastee eight, and the Chefman six.

Presets set time and temperature for common foods. They help beginners but can feel limiting. App recipes add guidance. The Tastee lists 24 one-touch presets, the most here. Check how many presets are listed and whether manual control remains, because experienced cooks usually override presets, and bad presets burn food.

A dishwasher-safe basket saves time. Ceramic coatings still need soft sponges and no metal tools, since scratches shorten the life of the finish and let food stick. Confirm dishwasher-safe is stated on the listing, as on the Tastee. Handwashing is gentler on any coated basket.

faq.q: Is ceramic better than regular non-stick?
faq.a: Ceramic avoids traditional PTFE-based coatings, which some buyers prefer. Durability varies by brand, so treat it as a preference, not a guarantee. The TurboBlaze and Nuwave state PFAS-free outright, which is the clearest claim here.
Avoid them on any coated basket. Use silicone or wood utensils, since metal can scratch ceramic and shorten its life, whether the basket is on the Cosori or the Chefman, and wash gently.
For two or three people, yes. The Cosori Pro LE fits that need at 5 quarts. For four or more, step up to the TurboBlaze at 6 quarts or an 8 quart model, because a crowded basket cooks unevenly.

faq.q: How do I set up a new air fryer?
faq.a: Wash the basket, run it empty once, and leave space behind it for airflow. Place it on a heat-safe counter away from the wall, then read the manual for the first-use burn-off and any smell it mentions.

faq.q: How do I clean the basket?
faq.a: Use warm soapy water and a soft sponge unless the manual says dishwasher-safe, as on the Tastee. Avoid scouring pads, since they can damage a ceramic finish and shorten its life.

Models with a bake function, such as the Cosoris, can handle small batches in the basket. Check the Chefman and Nuwave listings for baking modes, because the Nuwave names few functions and the Chefman lists six in all.

finalTake: Buy the TurboBlaze for a household of three or four. Pick the Pro LE for one to three people on a tighter budget, and the Nuwave Brio Plus when big batches matter. If PFAS-free is a deciding factor, choose a model that says so outright.
